I will still farm the way I know best: I start from what I did last year, then I look at what the better fields around me did. On my 16.9 mu, cotton will still take the biggest share because that is the crop I know best and I have well water, so I can hold it if the weather turns dry. I will not cut fertilizer too hard. Fertilizer costs money, that is true, but if I save a few yuan and the field comes out weak, that loss is bigger. So I will feed cotton a bit heavier, wheat and maize steady like before, and mungbean lighter because it does not need as much. I will use improved or hybrid seed where I have seen neighbors get a good stand and better picking or better ears; I do not change just because somebody talks nice, I change when I see it work in nearby land. For cotton I will plough first, put enough base fertilizer, water several times from the well, and spray more because insects and disease can climb fast. For wheat I will do the usual winter field work and give it three waters if the season asks for it. For maize I will keep it simple and feed it enough to push the ears. Mungbean I will spend less on, because it is a smaller crop for me and I do not want too much money tied up there. That is how I will spread my money and labor this year.
